definitions: So: used to introduce a clause that shows the result or consequence of the action or situation described in the main clause.
So that: used to introduce a clause that states the purpose of the action in the main clause.
Unless: used to introduce a condition that must be met for something else to happen or not happen; equivalent to 'if not'.
examples: It was raining, so we stayed inside.
She studied hard so that she would pass the exam.
You won't get a good grade unless you study.
